'''Chia-Chiao Lin''' ({{zh|t=林家翹}}; 7 July 1916&nbsp;– 13 January 2013) was a Chinese-born American [[Applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[List of institute professors at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology|Institute Professor]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.tsinghua.edu.cn/publish/news/4205/2013/20130113145751956660184/20130113145751956660184_.html|script-title=zh:著名科学家林家翘逝世 胡和平前往吊唁|date=2013-01-13|publisher=[[Tsinghua University]]|language=Chinese|accessdate=13 January 2013|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130116145842/http://news.tsinghua.edu.cn/publish/news/4205/2013/20130113145751956660184/20130113145751956660184_.html|archivedate=16 January 2013}}</ref>

Lin made major contributions to the theory of [[hydrodynamic stability]], [[turbulent flow]], [[mathematics]], and [[astrophysics]].

==Biography==
Lin was born in [[Beijing]] with ancestral roots in [[Fuzhou]]. In 1937 Lin graduated from the department of physics, [[Tsinghua University]] in Beijing. 

After graduation he was a [[teaching assistant]] in the Tsinghua University physics department. In 1939 Lin won a [[Boxer Indemnity Scholarship]] and was initially supported to study in the [[United Kingdom]]. However, due to [[World War II]], Lin and several others were sent to [[North America]] by ship. Unluckily, Lin's ship was stopped in [[Kobe]], [[Empire of Japan|Japan]], and all students had to return to China. 

In 1940, Lin finally reached [[Canada]] and studied at the [[University of Toronto]] from which he earned his M.Sc. In 1941. Lin continued his studies in the [[United States]] and received his PhD from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1944 under [[Theodore von Kármán]]. His PhD thesis provided an analytic method to solve a problem in the stability of parallel shearing flows, which was the subject of [[Werner Heisenberg]]'s PhD thesis.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aas.org/obituaries/chia-chiao-lin-1916-2013|title=Chia-Chiao Lin (1916 - 2013) |publisher= American Astronomical Society|work=Obituaries|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181228083136/https://aas.org/obituaries/chia-chiao-lin-1916-2013|archive-date=2018-12-28|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Lin also taught at Caltech between 1943 and 1945. He taught at [[Brown University]] between 1945 and 1947. Lin joined the faculty of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1947. Lin was promoted to professor at [[MIT]] in 1953 and became an [[Institute Professor]] of [[MIT]] in 1963. He was President of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] from 1972 to 1974.<ref>[http://www.siam.org/about/more/presidents.php Society of Industrial and Applied Mathematics records]</ref> Lin retired from MIT in 1987.  

In 2002, he moved back to China and helped found the Zhou Pei-Yuan Center for Applied Mathematics (ZCAM) at Tsinghua University. He died in [[Beijing]] in 2013, aged 96.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-01-14 |title=Pioneering applied mathematician Chia-Chiao Lin dies at 96 |url=https://news.mit.edu/2013/obit-chia-chiao-lin |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=MIT News {{!}} Massachusetts Institute of Technology |language=en}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
During his career Lin has received many prizes and awards, including:
* The first [[Fluid Dynamics Prize]] (from the [[American Physical Society]], in 1979)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?name=Chia%20Chiao%20Lin |title=Fluid Dynamics Prize |publisher=Amperican Physical Society |accessdate=2007-12-02}}</ref>
*The 1976 NAS Award in Applied Mathematics and Numerical Analysis<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_NAS_Award_Applied_Mathematics |title=NAS Award in Applied Mathematics and Numerical Analysis |publisher=[[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]] |accessdate=2007-12-02 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927204508/http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_NAS_Award_Applied_Mathematics |archivedate=2007-09-27 }}</ref>
* The 1975 [[Timoshenko Medal]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asme.org/Governance/Honors/SocietyAwards/Timoshenko_Medal.cfm |title=Timoshenko Medal |publisher=American Society of Mechanical Engineers |accessdate=2007-12-02}}</ref>
* The 1973 [[Otto Laporte Award]]
* Caltech's Distinguished Alumni Award<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.eas.caltech.edu/engenious/fall03/alumni.html |title=Distinguished Alumni Award |publisher=California Institute of Technology |accessdate=2007-12-02 |archive-date=2008-07-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080725173551/http://www.eas.caltech.edu/engenious/fall03/alumni.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Lin was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chia-Chiao Lin |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/chia-chiao-lin-dottg0/ |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chia-Chiao Lin |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/chia-chiao-lin |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |language=en}}</ref> and the [[American Philosophical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Member History |url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Chia-Chiao+Lin&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref> cited in the [[American Men and Women of Science]]. and a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. Lin was elected Academician of [[Academia Sinica]] in 1958, and became a Foreign Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1994.
